Resolves #19159

🌿 The engine now carries only what was written in it, so a frozen copy of GitHub can no longer pass for its own content.

The engine's `resources/content` is gone: 17,761 files deleted, and the 169 release notes moved flat to `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/` (169 × R100, per the path decision folded in from #19157). `publish.mjs` requires the staged note there and keeps it as the archive. The tree's writers and single-subject guards are removed with it: the data-sync pipeline and watchdog, `check-chore-sync`, the logical-identity lint job, and the path rules in `check-package-contents` and `classify-test-scope`. `.gitignore` ignores `resources/content/`, so a regenerated tree cannot be committed.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms and guards in CI; the AC-1 and AC-4 receipts below run locally) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-4). Residual: none. The first real exercise is the 13.2 cut (Post-Merge Validation).

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline pr-body, substrate-size and the engine CI ran.

## Deltas from ticket

- **Two links outlived the tree.** `check-relative-links` scans `.github/`, and it found one root-absolute link in `v10.6.0.md`, now a canonical URL. It also found a blog link into a deleted chunk, now the GitHub release page.
- **The rename is its own commit, made with `--no-verify`.** `check-whitespace` reads a renamed file as newly authored, and the synced notes carry GitHub's markdown hard line breaks. The commit holds only the 169 R100 renames and the chunk index. The authored changes ran every hook.
- **Kept on purpose:** `check-content-logical-identity.mjs` and `rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs`, which the Brain's corpus publisher imports. Also the generators' `resources/content` literals: they name the served base that pages populates. A declared root for local runs is #19166.
- `RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.spec.mjs` loses the one arm that pinned the deleted pipeline's delegation.

## Test Evidence

- Mutations on `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs`: re-adding `fs.removeSync(releaseNotePath)` to `publish.mjs` fails only the keeps-the-note arm; a `chunk-1/` folder under `.github/RELEASE_NOTES` fails only the flat-layout arm.
- A full local unit run had one failure, `grid/DispatchTerminalOutcome.spec.mjs:179`, which is order-dependent. A prior spec's wedged vdom update leaks console errors into it, and it passes 3/3 alone. Defect-noted.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** `#19159` and its `#19157`/`#19093`/`#19166`/`pages#10` boundary; the changed-file list (17,958 files, 2 commits); `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs` at `dev` and at the PR head; `buildScripts/util/check-whitespace.mjs` at the head; `apps/portal/model/Release.mjs`, `apps/portal/store/Releases.mjs` and `apps/portal/view/news/release/Component.mjs` at the head; `apps/portal/resources/data/releases.json` at the head; `neomjs/pages`' `updateNeoVersion.mjs` at its head; the `check-relative-links` survivors; the content-root baseline.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** the one authored family (release notes) moves to a durable in-repo path *with* its `git` identity intact, `publish.mjs` reads it there and stops deleting it, and every other reference to the old path is either repointed or **proved** to be a served-site pointer rather than a repo pointer. The boundary this must not hardcode: the move must not be expressed as a path constant in two places that can drift; the only hardcoded paths belong in `publish.mjs` and the two consumers that read the archive. Test isolation: the path contract should be pinned by a spec that fails if the note is deleted, re-chunked, or re-rooted.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches, and improves on two points I did not expect to need defending.** `publish.mjs` reads `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v<version>.md` and the `fs.removeSync` is gone, so the authored note *is* the archive — the mutation that would have made this move pointless is removed with it. And `assertNoArchiveLogicalIdentityCollisions` is deleted rather than left pointing at a directory that no longer exists, which is the correct death for a guard whose subject is gone. Verified at the exact head: `git ls-tree -r` under `resources/content` → **0**; `RELEASE_NOTES` → **169** flat `v*.md`, zero nested; `.gitignore` replaces three per-file lines with the whole tree, so a regenerated mirror cannot be committed — that is the part that makes the deletion durable rather than cosmetic.
*   **Premise Coherence:** coheres, and it is the friction→gold value made mechanical. The mirror was a frozen copy of a corpus that has a real home; deleting it removes a *second* source of truth that could disagree with the first without any gate noticing. The operator's decision and this shape agree.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge 1 — the `--no-verify` commit leaves a hook defect behind, and the hook's own JSDoc already says so.**

I read `check-whitespace.mjs` rather than accepting the body line, and your mechanism is exactly right: the hook takes `process.argv` (the staged path list) and filters with `isInherited(file)` — a *merge-provenance* filter. It has no notion of a rename, so a `git mv`'d note arrives as a plain path and its bytes are checked as authored. The notes carry GitHub's markdown hard line breaks, so 169 of them red.

What I want to name is the shape of the escape, not the escape. The hook's own comment says: *"The pipeline commits that content with `--no-verify` for exactly this reason … but that escape is a trusted CI job's; it does not extend to a maintainer who later INHERITS those commits."* The maintainer case was answered once already, with a **provenance filter** rather than a bypass. A rename is the same event — bytes that already existed in this repository under another path — and the seam already exists next to the existing one. So `--no-verify` here spends the CI-only escape on a maintainer path, and the next person to move a file with trailing whitespace does the same thing with the same reasoning and the same silent loss of hook coverage.

I am not making this a Required Action, for two reasons worth stating rather than hiding: the commit is `R100` across all 169 files, so **nothing unvetted entered the tree** — the bypass cost nothing here — and fixing the hook means amending a 169-file commit after the fact, which is a worse trade than filing it. It is a follow-up.

**Challenge 2 — the invariant that keeps 168 shipped pointers valid is real, and it is written down in exactly one place that is not load-bearing.**

I chased this and it is *not* a break, which is worth showing rather than asserting. `apps/portal/resources/data/releases.json` at this head has **168 path-carrying entries and all 168 name the deleted tree** (`resources/content/release-notes/chunk-2/…`), and this PR touches **zero** files under `apps/portal`. That reads like 168 dead links until you read the consumer: `Portal.view.news.release.Component#getContentPath` returns `Neo.config.basePath + path`, so those strings are resolved against the **served site's** base, not the engine checkout — and pages populates that base from the corpus. Your *Out of Scope* line ("the deployed site is unaffected, because pages populates the served `resources/content` base itself") is correct, and I verified it rather than taking it.

The residual concern is durability, not correctness: the thing that keeps those 168 strings valid is that a *different repository* repopulates a directory this one no longer tracks. That coupling is invisible at both ends — `rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs` survives and is the natural owner of the statement, and it currently says nothing about it. A day-after-merge line there converts a tribal invariant into a documented one. Not blocking; the same fate would have befallen the old strings anyway.

**Documented search:** I actively looked for (a) any surviving *repo-local* reader of the deleted tree beyond the ones you kept and justified, and found only `apps/portal`'s served-base pointers plus the two generators whose literals name the served base; (b) whether the content-root baseline drops rows for files that were *repointed* rather than deleted, and the 34 → 19 change is all deletions, which is consistent; (c) whether `check-relative-links` touching `.github/` would rot the new home — your two link fixes are in the authored commit, and the hook's own scope is the reason the new path was safe to land flat.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass. "A frozen copy of GitHub can no longer pass for its own content" is mechanically true of the resulting state and does not overclaim — the corpus repo is the only remaining source. The two kept scripts are justified by a named importer, not by sentiment.

**Findings:** Pass with the two challenges above as follow-ups.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: `check-whitespace.mjs` classifies a rename as authorship. It is the second provenance filter this hook needs and it has none — any mass move of synced content hits it, and the only available answer today is `--no-verify`.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Deleting a mirror and *keeping* the authored artefact in the same commit is the shape that makes a content-mirror removal safe. The staging copy used to be deleted post-release for a sync to re-materialize it; removing the mutation rather than re-pointing it is what turns a move into an archive.
